title: Positive cohomology of a dense-open complement after open restriction
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field, f:X -> Spec k a separated finite-type curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], U a dense open of X [def-weil-open-immersion], and i:Z -> X a closed immersion with image X minus U [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For any commutative coefficient ring Lambda and Lambda-module etale sheaf G on Z [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], every open immersion a:W -> X satisfies H^q(W,a^{-1}(forget(i_*G)))=0 for all q>0, where direct image, inverse image and cohomology are [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Neither G nor its stalks need to be torsion or constructible.

proof.text: Apply dense_open_finite_complement to U. Set V = a inverse-image U. Injectivity of the open immersion a makes the inverse image of the finite complement finite. For each point x outside V, injectivity identifies the inverse image of the singleton {a(x)} with {x}, so continuity gives closedness. The residue-field map of an open immersion is an isomorphism, transporting separable closedness to the residue field at x.

The composite V -> W -> X has range in U, disjoint from the range of i. Thus its module inverse image of i_*G is zero by open-closed vanishing. Apply the coefficient-forgetting functor, which is additive sectionwise and hence preserves zero objects. The natural inverse-image/forget isomorphism and the inverse-image composition isomorphism identify this zero object with the restriction to V of the displayed abelian sheaf on W.

Write every positive q as n+1 and apply the existing finite-support acyclicity theorem on W to V and the displayed sheaf. Its hypotheses are exactly the finite complement, closedness, separably closed residue fields, and zero restriction obtained above. This treats empty opens and complements and arbitrary commutative coefficient rings without a torsion assumption.
